rules.title: Application screening fee capped at actual costs and $30 (CPI-adjusted), with refund and availability limits
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only up to its actual out-of-pocket screening costs, and never more than $30 per applicant adjusted yearly for CPI since 1998 (listed as $68.96 for 2026). The landlord must give you an itemized receipt, refund any unused portion, and give you a copy of your credit report within 7 days. It cannot charge a fee if no unit is or will soon be available, and must either consider applications in the order received and approve the first qualified applicant, or refund the full fee to applicants not selected within 7 days of selection or 30 days of applying, whichever comes first.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually from 1998-01-01 ($68.96 for 2026 per Berkeley)
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property in California and their agents who charge rental applicants, including guarantors and cosigners, a fee to screen an application.
rules.exemptions: Under the first-come process, no refund is required for an applicant denied after consideration for failing the landlord's written screening criteria. Does not preempt deposit and fee rules under federal or state housing assistance programs.
rules.reason: All five candidates describe provisions of Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (fee cap, receipts and credit report, availability limit, and the first-come or refund rule), so they were merged into one record citing the official statute text. The 2026-01-01 date in D026 appears to be an amendment or adjustment date rather than when the $30 cap began, so effective_date is left null.
